text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentThis Is What Happens When 1,000 People Bury Their Underwear for ScienceTalk about getting to the bottom of thingsJCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CDT on August 27, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleSoil is alive. It’s chock-full of bacteria, fungi, earthworms, and other dirt-dwelling critters. These living things recycle organic matter, aerate the soil, and churn out nutrients, all of which contribute to a fertile ecosystem. Without them, plants struggle to grow. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Nonverbal Communication In Space | NASA AstronautsShareNextStayBut how do you tell just how alive your soil is? According to a new study in the journal Plants, People, Planet, you bury your underwear.  Ecologists from the University of Zurich enlisted more than 1,000 citizen scientists (half of them farmers) to participate in the project, designed to measure the health of soil across Switzerland. They were each mailed a packet containing two (clean) pairs of undies, 12 teabags, and a baggie for soil samples. They also received detailed instructions directing them to dig holes in different locations, take a soil sample, bury the underwear and tea bags, and then leave them for either 30 or 60 days. After that, they dug up their buried treasure, snapped some photos, and mailed everything to the lab.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
